names.official: State income tax on individuals (national income tax and tax on capital income)
names.native: Statlig inkomstskatt och skatt på kapital

taxes.base: Earned income above a threshold (national income tax) and capital income (a flat tax).

rate.headline: 20% above SEK 643,000 (2026); 30% on capital income
details: Employment income: 0% national income tax to SEK 643,000 and 20% above, on top of the average municipal tax of 32% (2026). Capital income is generally taxed at a flat 30% (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (reviews of August and September 2026), not checked against the Swedish Tax Agency (Skatteverket).

instruments.explanation: The National Tax List gives one line for the income taxes of individuals (SEK 854 billion). Eurostat’s accounts place SEK 726 billion of it with the municipalities and regions (their proportional income tax) and the rest with the State.

names.official: Taxes on occupational and non-occupational pension schemes and pension savings

taxes.base: As named in the National Tax List (occupational pensions defined benefit SEK 9.3 billion, defined contribution 8.5 billion, unit-linked 5.8 billion; non-occupational individual life insurance 5.6 billion, unit-linked 2.3 billion, individual pension saving 0.7 billion); the list does not state the tax base.

rate.headline: Set by the Yield Tax Act

instruments.explanation: Six lines that the list books as taxes on holding gains of households.

names.official: Corporate income tax

taxes.base: Profit of companies and other legal persons.

details: Taxable income is subject to corporate tax at a flat rate of 20.6% (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (reviews of August and September 2026), not checked against the Swedish Tax Agency (Skatteverket).

instruments.explanation: SEK 223.5 billion in 2024.

names.official: General payroll tax (the non-earmarked part of the employers’ social fees)

taxes.base: Remuneration to employees (and the earnings of the self-employed).

rate.headline: Part of the 31.42% employer fees
details: Mandatory social charges payable by employers on remuneration are levied at approximately 31.42% in all (PwC); the shares of the lines in the National Tax List are consistent with the general payroll tax being the largest component of that rate.

instruments.explanation: The National Tax List books the employers’ fees as taxes on payroll, not as social contributions; this is the largest line, SEK 274 billion.

names.official: Employers’ fees for sickness insurance, the labour market, parental insurance, survivors’ pensions and industrial injuries

taxes.base: Remuneration to employees. Sickness insurance SEK 82.6 billion, parental insurance 60.5 billion, labour market 57.9 billion, survivors’ pension 14.0 billion, industrial injuries 4.7 billion, and small lines including a negative miscellaneous line of SEK 3.5 billion.

rate.headline: Part of the 31.42% employer fees
details: Mandatory social charges payable by employers are levied at approximately 31.42%; since 1 January 2024 the lower rates for young people have been removed (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (reviews of August and September 2026), not checked against the Swedish Tax Agency (Skatteverket).

instruments.explanation: Statistically booked as payroll taxes, but in Sweden the money is earmarked for the social insurances.

names.official: Part of the pension fee paid to the State budget
names.common: Pension fee to the State budget

taxes.base: As named in the National Tax List: the part of the employers’ pension fee that goes to the State budget rather than to the pension funds.

instruments.explanation: The rest of the pension fee is in the social contributions (the compulsory employers’ pension fees to the pension funds).

names.official: Special payroll tax and the tax on salaried employees’ life insurance

taxes.base: Pension premiums and pension costs beyond the mandatory system, and life insurance for salaried employees.

rate.headline: About 24% on additional pension premiums
details: A special salary tax is levied at approximately 24% on pension premiums beyond the mandatory system (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (reviews of August and September 2026), not checked against the Swedish Tax Agency (Skatteverket).

instruments.explanation: SEK 65 billion in 2024.

legalRefs.locator: sheet SE, D29C C03 and C04

names.official: Employers’ compulsory pension fees (to the pension funds)

taxes.base: Remuneration to employees.

instruments.explanation: The part of the mandatory pension fee that the list books as a social contribution (SEK 165 billion); the part paid to the State budget is in the payroll lines above.

names.official: Employers’ voluntary pension fees (occupational pensions) and other voluntary contributions

taxes.base: Premiums for occupational pensions agreed in collective agreements (SEK 52.1 billion) and other voluntary contributions (SEK 0.1 billion).

rate.headline: Set by collective agreements
details: The National Tax List includes them because they are close to compulsory in practice; PwC notes that pension benefits beyond the mandatory system are customary among most Swedish employers.

instruments.explanation: Included in the list although they are agreed, not legislated.

names.official: Compulsory pension contributions of the self-employed

taxes.base: The income of the self-employed.

instruments.explanation: SEK 3.2 billion; the list gives no employees’ contributions for Sweden, because the employees’ pension charge is collected as part of the income tax.

names.official: Value added tax (central government part and the part passed to the EU)

taxes.base: Goods and services supplied in Sweden and imports.
taxes.payer: Consumers; businesses charge it and claim input credits.

rate.headline: 25% standard; 12% and 6% reduced
details: The general VAT rate is 25% on most goods and services; 12% on hotel accommodation, foodstuffs, restaurant meals and low- or non-alcoholic drinks; 6% on newspapers, books, passenger transport and others (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (reviews of August and September 2026), not checked against the Swedish Tax Agency (Skatteverket).

instruments.explanation: The largest tax: SEK 548 billion for the central government and SEK 8 billion booked as the EU part.

names.official: Import duties and levies on imported alcoholic beverages

taxes.base: Goods imported from outside the EU, by the Common Customs Tariff.

rate.headline: EU Common Customs Tariff
details: An EU own resource; Eurostat records it under the EU institutions.

instruments.explanation: Collected for the EU budget.

names.official: Taxes on fuel (energy and carbon dioxide taxes) and the tax on sulphur

taxes.base: Petrol, diesel and other fuels, by quantity.
taxes.payer: Fuel suppliers; passed on at the pump.

rate.headline: Per litre, with an energy and a CO₂ component

instruments.explanation: SEK 40.1 billion.

legalRefs.locator: sheet SE, D214A C01 and C02

names.official: Tax on electrical power

taxes.base: Electricity consumed.

instruments.explanation: SEK 31.2 billion.

names.official: Taxes on alcoholic beverages and on tobacco

taxes.base: Alcoholic beverages (SEK 18.0 billion) and tobacco (SEK 14.8 billion).
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Per litre of alcohol; per unit of tobacco

instruments.explanation: Two lines.

legalRefs.locator: sheet SE, D214A C04 and C05

names.official: Taxes on chemicals, pesticides, waste, plastic bags and gravel, and other excise duties
names.native: Skatt på kemikalier, bekämpningsmedel, avfall, plastpåsar och naturgrus
names.common: Chemicals, waste and other environmental taxes

taxes.base: Excise duty on chemicals (SEK 2.5 billion), waste (SEK 0.4 billion), plastic bags (SEK 0.4 billion), pesticides, other chemicals and gravel, and a small negative line of other excises.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers of the products.

instruments.explanation: Seven small environmental taxes.

legalRefs.locator: sheet SE, D214L C02, C04, C05, C08, D214A C06–C08

names.official: Stamp duty on mortgages and registrations of property, aircraft and vessels

taxes.base: Mortgage deeds and the registration of title to property (SEK 10.5 billion), corporate mortgages and registrations (SEK 0.2 billion), aircraft and vessels.

rate.headline: A percentage of the price or the mortgage

instruments.explanation: Sweden’s tax on property transactions: SEK 10.6 billion.

names.official: Tax on gambling, surplus from gambling, profits of the alcohol monopoly and lottery licences
names.native: Lotteriskatt; överskott från spel; Systembolagets vinst

taxes.base: Tax on gambling (SEK 4.8 billion), the State’s surplus from gambling (SEK 1.6 billion), the profits of the alcohol retail monopoly (SEK 0.4 billion) and lottery licences (SEK 0.05 billion).

rate.headline: Set by the gambling and alcohol laws

instruments.explanation: Four lines.

legalRefs.locator: sheet SE, D214F C03, D214J, D29E C03

names.official: Tax on traffic insurance premiums and the flight tax

taxes.base: Traffic insurance premiums (SEK 2.8 billion) and air passengers (SEK 1.7 billion).
taxes.payer: Insurers and airlines; passed on to customers.

rate.headline: A percentage of premiums; a set amount per passenger

instruments.explanation: Two lines.

legalRefs.locator: sheet SE, D214G C01, D214H C02

names.official: Motor vehicle tax and road tax (households and enterprises), the fee for lorries and electricity capacity fees

taxes.base: Motor vehicles paid by households (SEK 9.6 billion) and enterprises (SEK 5.0 billion), road tax paid by households (SEK 1.5 billion) and enterprises (SEK 1.3 billion), the fee for lorries (SEK 1.5 billion) and a small capacity fee.

rate.headline: By vehicle weight, fuel and emissions

instruments.explanation: Six lines.

legalRefs.locator: sheet SE, D59D C01 and C02, D29B C01 and C03, D29F C03, D29E C05

names.official: Tax on real estate

taxes.base: Buildings and land by assessed value.

rate.headline: A percentage of assessed value, with a cap for homes
details: The list does not give rates.

instruments.explanation: SEK 41.4 billion. Eurostat books it under central government, although part of the fee for homes is a municipal fee.

names.official: Public service fee paid by households

taxes.base: Individuals with income, to finance public service television and radio.

rate.headline: A percentage of income up to a cap

instruments.explanation: SEK 8.9 billion in 2024.

names.official: Risk tax, resolution fee, deposit insurance fee and other small fees

taxes.base: The risk tax on credit institutions (SEK 6.7 billion), the resolution fee (SEK 4.3 billion), the deposit insurance fee (SEK 2.3 billion), the fee for the discharge of nitrogen (SEK 0.6 billion), the telecommunications fee and waste incineration.

instruments.explanation: Six lines.

legalRefs.locator: sheet SE, D29H C02, C04–C07, D29F C05

names.official: Municipal and regional income tax on individuals

taxes.base: The same earned income as the State income tax: wages, pensions and business income of residents.

rate.headline: Average 32% (2026), set by each municipality and region
details: The average municipal income tax rate is 32% (PwC); municipalities and regions each set their own rate.

instruments.explanation: SEK 726 billion, 85% of the income tax on individuals in the list. It is a proportional tax collected with the State tax.
